report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

hypotheses.pattern: Three modules each claim a guard is 'advisory only' and must never block an autonomous action, but only one module carries a flag that callers could honor; the other two rely on caller discipline that no shared mechanism enforces.
hypotheses.refuted_if: A single shared advisory flag or registry is defined and all three gates read it, or if callers are all in one module that already treats all three as advisory.

hypotheses.pattern: Two modules claim a digest protects against hand-editing derived lists, but the digest is defined in neither chunk and the validation logic is absent from both, so the guarantee is duplicated without being implemented in any visible location.
hypotheses.refuted_if: A shared digest module is visible elsewhere and both chunks import it, or if the digest logic is actually present in the omitted remainder of one of these files.

hypotheses.pattern: Two modules each claim to fail open when git cannot answer (tarball checkout), citing the same reasoning and the same sibling module, but neither chunk contains the fail-open logic — the guarantee is asserted in two places and implemented in neither.
hypotheses.refuted_if: The fail-open branch is present in the remainder of snapshot_freshness or inventory_freshness, or if both modules share a helper that implements it.

hypotheses.pattern: Two modules claim to 'report' a degradation (empty type vocabulary, empty package list) rather than silently treating it as 'nothing changed', but both implementations return an empty set/list without any reporting mechanism visible in either chunk.
hypotheses.refuted_if: Either module has a logging call or a side-channel in the omitted body, or if the caller is required to check the empty result and report it.

hypotheses.pattern: Two modules claim a gate is 'never raises' and returns refusals, but both have code paths that can raise exceptions not caught in the visible portion, and neither chunk shows the full exception handling.
hypotheses.refuted_if: The omitted bodies wrap all risky calls in try/except or the registry functions are documented to never raise.

hypotheses.pattern: Two modules claim a check covers 'all of it' (digest covers every field, scanner covers three layers), but the implementations are cut off or absent, so the coverage claim is duplicated without verification in either chunk.
hypotheses.refuted_if: The full implementations are visible elsewhere and demonstrably enumerate all fields/layers.
